clue.text: Swift attack, seizing power

indicators.note: the attack seizes, or grips, the power symbol, so it goes around it

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A rapid assault that grabs control of the electricity supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid and swift are synonyms, both meaning very fast.

clue.text: Doctor brought up thinner substance to be injected

indicators.note: the substance goes inside the reversed word, as an injection goes in
in a down clue, brought up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: rarer means thinner, as of air
the gist is the substance or essence of something

explanation.surface: A doctor raised a diluting fluid to inject into a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns RARER into RERAR, and 'to be injected' puts GIST into it.
explanation.definitionFit: In UK hospitals a registrar is a senior grade of doctor below consultant.

clue.text: Turn to somebody for a lift

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting means the letters are read upwards, back to front

parts.note: taken as written
a VIP is a somebody, an important person

explanation.surface: Turning to a person for a ride in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a lift' turns TO VIP upwards to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To pivot is to turn on a point.

clue.text: Depicter, shaky and infirm

indicators.note: shaky means unsteady, so the letters wobble into a new order

explanation.surface: A painter who is wobbly and frail.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepit means worn out and weak with age, synonymous with infirm.

clue.text: Thereby disposed of CIA post

indicators.note: disposed in the sense of arranged or set out, so these letters are laid out afresh

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone was got rid of from a job at the American intelligence agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed of' reads as 'got rid of', but 'disposed' is the anagram signal (arranged), and 'of' joins CIA and POST in the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means by that very fact, which is close to thereby in sense.

clue.text: Expression of surprise seeing Scottish island, not large

indicators.note: not means without, so the abbreviation for large is dropped

parts.note: Islay is an island of the Inner Hebrides, famous for whisky
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A gasp of astonishment on seeing a small Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: I say is an old-fashioned British exclamation of surprise.

clue.text: Perceive the true nature of help in time of need

definitions.meaning: to see past a pretence to the reality underneath
to support someone until a difficulty is over

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to detect a deception and to support someone through hardship.

clue.text: End up with heartless Scandinavian

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: Finnish means from Finland, often grouped with Scandinavia

explanation.surface: Ending up with a cruel Nordic person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes one of the central Ns of FINNISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish up somewhere is an idiom meaning to end up there.

clue.text: Accountant had to fix employee seeking favour

parts.note: CA stands for chartered accountant
to pin is to fix in place
a hand is a worker, as in farm hand

explanation.surface: An accountant had to sack a worker who was trying to curry favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fix' looks like an anagram signal, but it means PIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Going cap in hand is an idiom for humbly asking a favour, like a beggar.

clue.text: Young bird in a brace put up round fringes of lake

indicators.note: the reversed number goes round the letters from the lake
in a down clue, put up means read upwards, so back to front

parts.note: a brace is a pair, two

indicators.note: fringes of means the first and last letters of lake

explanation.surface: A fledgling in a pair of birds raised near the edge of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns the pair into OWT; 'round' then encloses the lake's first and last letters, so 'Young bird' is the definition, not the brace.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a baby owl, so a young bird.

clue.text: Set off in pursuit, dog finally achieves seizure

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word dog
a seizure is a fit or convulsion, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dog chasing something eventually manages to grab it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seizure' seems to be the dog's catch, but it is the anagram signal: G plus ACHIEVES is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To give chase is an idiom for starting to pursue someone or something.

clue.text: Style of writing about gangster in Asian country

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a pen can mean a writer's style, as in 'a caustic pen'
Al Capone is the crossword's stock gangster

explanation.surface: A literary style concerning a mobster set in an Asian land.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is a landlocked country in the Himalayas, an example of an Asian nation.

clue.text: Dog in pound released by colonist

indicators.note: the pound symbol is let go by the colonist, so it leaves the word

parts.note: a settler is someone who colonises new land
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A dog held in an animal pound is let out by a pioneer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like a dogs' home, but it is the letter L (the pound sign), dropped from SETTLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter is a breed of gun dog, so it is an example of a dog.

clue.text: Horse's breast and head are brown

parts.note: the chest is the breast
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A description of a horse whose chest and head are brown.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse's sets the scene and hints at the answer, which is also a horse of that colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Chestnut is a reddish-brown colour, the shade of a horse chestnut's seed.

clue.text: Angry commander's vehicle seen in island

parts.note: mad means angry
an aga is a Turkish commander
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A furious officer's car is spotted on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Madagascar is a large island off the east coast of Africa.

clue.text: Varying reports about army and protective equipment

indicators.note: the reshuffled letters go about, or around, the army
varying means changing, so the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the IRA is the Irish Republican Army

explanation.surface: Differing accounts concerning the military and its safety gear.
explanation.walkthrough: IRA, the Irish Republican Army, is a crossword staple for 'army'; 'about' puts it inside the rearranged letters (RESPTOR).
explanation.definitionFit: A respirator is a mask worn to protect the wearer's breathing, so it is protective equipment.

clue.text: View ecstatic people in it

parts.note: sent is old slang for thrilled, carried away

indicators.note: the people are placed inside the word it

parts.note: men means people

explanation.surface: An opinion on joyous folk caught up in something.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentiment is a view or opinion.

clue.text: Pop piece

definitions.meaning: to pop something is British slang for to ... it, as in the song about popping the weasel
a chess piece of the lowest value

explanation.definitionFit: To pop is to hock goods; the lowest chessman is also called this.

clue.text: Point to pre eminent feature of Ursa Minor

parts.note: north is a point of the compass
star means leading or outstanding

explanation.surface: Pointing to the most prominent thing in the Little Bear constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris, the pole star, is the brightest star in Ursa Minor, the Little Bear.

clue.text: Greek biographer removing one plant climbing gateway?

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means read upwards
the plant has the numeral one taken away

parts.note: a tulip is a plant
I is the Roman numeral for one
an arch may be a gateway, the question mark flagging an example

explanation.surface: A Greek writer takes away a climbing plant from a gate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' takes I from TULIP, giving TULP, and 'climbing' turns that into PLUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Plutarch wrote the Parallel Lives of famous Greeks and Romans.

clue.text: Standing in line

definitions.meaning: a row of soldiers or a taxi stand line

explanation.definitionFit: Rank means status or position, and also a row, such as soldiers in rank.

clue.text: Aircraft may be held with raging storm

indicators.note: to storm is to rush about wildly, so these letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An aircraft might be grounded because of a fierce storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raging' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder with HELD; 'storm' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hang-glider is an unpowered flying craft, an example of an aircraft.

clue.text: Tom's family, one up a tree?

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
kin means family

explanation.surface: A tomcat's relatives, one stuck up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one up a tree' suggests a stranded cat, but means a dangling flower spike on a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A catkin is a hanging flower spike on trees such as willow or hazel.

clue.text: Delivery of pottery to 16, perhaps

parts.note: china is fine pottery
a pawn, the answer to 16, is one example of a chessman, so a man

explanation.surface: Bringing crockery to someone, maybe at number sixteen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' suggests a parcel, but in cricket a chinaman is a ball bowled by a left-arm wrist spinner.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket this word names a type of ball, so a kind of delivery by the bowler.

clue.text: Game fish

definitions.meaning: a simple game of throwing and ... a ball
to fish is to try to land something on a line

explanation.definitionFit: It names a ball game for children and also a verb for landing fish.

clue.text: Pain beginning to strike small person

indicators.note: beginning to points at the first letter of strike

parts.note: titch is British slang for a small person

explanation.surface: Discomfort starting to hit a little person.
explanation.walkthrough: TITCH is everyday British slang for a small person.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch is a sharp pain in the side, felt when running.

clue.text: Kid's dad has abandoned patron saint

indicators.note: the father has left, so his letters go from the saint's name

parts.note: Patrick is the patron saint of Ireland
pa is dad

explanation.surface: A child's father has walked out on the patron saint.
explanation.definitionFit: To kid someone is to trick them.

clue.text: The thread of the story

definitions.meaning: spun fibre for knitting or weaving
a long tale, often an exaggerated one

explanation.definitionFit: It means spun fibre and also a tall tale told by a storyteller.

clue.text: Adjust temperature lacking in intensity

parts.note: weak means feeble or lacking strength

explanation.surface: Turn the heat control slightly because it is not strong enough.
explanation.definitionFit: To tweak something is to make a small adjustment to it.

clue.text: Swiss registration applied to relief flight for transportation of skiers

parts.note: CH, for Confoederatio Helvetica, is the international vehicle code of Switzerland
an airlift is a supply flight bringing relief

explanation.surface: A Swiss-registered aircraft is used in an aid flight that carries skiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairlift carries skiers up the slope on seats hanging from a cable.

clue.text: I'd hurt Nan badly, in an accident

indicators.note: badly means the letters are put into poor order

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe giving no letter
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to injuring their grandmother seriously in a mishap.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit-and-run is a road accident where the driver leaves the scene.

clue.text: One rambling about old president in time

indicators.note: the president is put in the abbreviation for time

parts.note: HR is the abbreviation for hour, a unit of time
Ike was the nickname of US president Dwight Eisenhower

explanation.surface: Someone wandering around a former president for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiker is a walker, and rambling about is walking for pleasure.
